turns.t: Hello, Mr Stone, I'm Kate, the nurse. The doctor asked me to do your psoriasis review with her. How are your skin and joints?
Um, hi. I'm not sure there's much to say. It's a bit better. Sorry, I get nervous. ~
No need to be. Where is it at the moment?
Elbows mainly, and a bit on the scalp. Scaly patches. They've shrunk since the summer.
That's good. Are you getting any joint pain or stiffness?
No. No, my joints are fine.
Hello, Mr Stone. Kate's updated me. Can I just look at the elbows? ~
Of course.
They've improved a lot since I last saw them, and I'm pleased. ~
That's good, isn't it? ~
Yes, very. What are you doing for them these days? ~
Nothing, really. Just moisturising. ~
That's fine, that's what I'd hoped you'd manage. The sunshine over the summer probably helped. ~
We went to Spain. ~
There you are. And how is your mood, are you coping all right? Psoriasis can get you down. ~
A bit nervous, but fine. ~
It's very common to feel self-conscious. Do you want some information on a support group? ~
Maybe. Yes, please. ~
I'll print it for you. ~
Mr Stone, the key thing is to keep moisturising every day, especially after a bath.
Right. I do it every night. ~
Good. Avoid scratching, and keep your nails short. Try not to pick at the scalp.
Okay. ~
And remember sunscreen, on the bits that aren't affected. ~
I'll remember. ~
Right, I'm happy with you today. If it flares up again, or you get any joint pain or swelling, or your nails start changing, come back and we'll treat it.
I will. Thank you. ~
Here's the leaflet, Mr Stone. ~
Thanks, Kate. Bye, doctor. ~
Take care. ~
